title: APO Pork Chops with Grape and Sage Gravy
description: Lean pork cutlets steam gently and finish in a smooth purple grape gravy infused with sage.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with food probe, bottom drip pan and middle wire rack

ingredients.name: lean boneless center-cut pork loin chops
ingredients.note: Trim the fat edge and cut horizontally into 1/2-inch cutlets.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water without a vegetable seasoning blend.

ingredients.name: red seedless grapes
ingredients.note: Halve lengthwise for cooking; strain out skins.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Fill the water tank and install the bottom drip pan. Preheat to 155°F with sous vide mode on, 100% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the food probe target to 145°F.

steps.title: Probe the cutlets
steps.text: Arrange {pork} unbagged in the shallow pan on the middle rack. Insert the probe parallel to the pan into the center of the thickest cutlet. Begin cooking immediately and set a separate 12-minute reminder for the first temperature check; respond sooner if the probe signals.

steps.title: Poach the grapes
steps.text: While the pork steams, simmer {grapes}, {sage} and {broth} in the covered HexClad over medium-low for 6–8 minutes until the grapes collapse.

steps.title: Strain the grape base
steps.text: Remove the sage. Press the cooked grapes and liquid through a fine sieve into a bowl, discarding all skins. Return the smooth base to the skillet and stir in {balsamic}.

steps.title: Make the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and keep it bubbling gently for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the gravy
steps.text: Swirl {butter} into the gravy off heat.

steps.title: Steam the pork
steps.text: Cook for about 15–35 minutes, checking at 12 minutes, until every cutlet reaches 145°F.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Remove the pan and rest the cutlets loosely covered in their juices for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Serve with the pork
steps.text: Slice the rested pork across the grain. Spoon the grape gravy onto each plate, nestle the slices into it and pour the rest over the top.

notes: Make ahead: Poach and strain the grapes a day ahead and refrigerate. Add the slurry at serving time. Option A adds balsamic. For gentler Option B, omit it and let the cooked grapes supply the flavor. For dairy-free gravy omit the butter. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the cutlets submerged in gravy for up to 2 months; the strained grape base reheats smoothly. Fridge reheat: Place one portion and its sauce in a shallow covered dish. Install the APO bottom drip pan and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off. Insert the probe in the coldest center and set it to 165°F. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw a single portion in the refrigerator overnight, then use the fridge reheating method. Stir the sauce until smooth.
